title: Remote Exercise iNtErvention for Wellbeing (RENEW) Trial
official: Remote Exercise iNtErvention for Wellbeing (RENEW) Trial: A 2-arm Randomized At-home, App-based Exercise Trial to Improve Adherence, Mental Health, and Wellbeing of British Columbian Healthcare Workers
summary: Healthcare workers report significantly worse mental health and wellbeing than the average employed Canadian. Evidence suggests that healthcare workers' leisure-time physical activity is associated with higher mental and physical health, while occupational physical activity is not. Our pilot work demonstrated that previously inactive healthcare workers who develop sustained off-site, at-home exercise routines using mobile applications (apps) have improved depressive symptoms and burnout, and lower rates of sick leave. Yet, in our work, only 23% of healthcare workers remained engaged with the apps for at least 80 or more minutes on average per week at the end of the 12-week study. In semi-structured interviews completed following their participation in the study, healthcare workers voiced their desire to have support from our team to help them maintain their motivation and improve their adherence. Here, we propose to conduct a randomized trial with two conditions of an aerobic exercise mobile app (using a suite of apps for whole body weight-based training, yoga, pilates, and barre) with or without support from a qualified exercise professional trained in motivational interviewing to improve healthcare workers' engagement with the suite of apps in their leisure time. In turn, we aim to improve their mental health and wellbeing as their exercise levels increase. By targeting adherence, our goal is to develop a feasible, engaging, and accessible solution that can be implemented as a more widely utilized program in the future, for healthcare workers and beyond.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Individuals over the age of 18
* Individuals who are employed/contracted by one of the 7 BC health authorities
* Individuals who are capable of and cleared for moderate physical activity, as assessed by CSEP's Get Active Questionnaire or a physician or a CSEP-certified Clinical Exercise Physiologist

Exclusion Criteria:

* Prospective participants must be cleared to participate in exercise. The CSEP-Get Active Questionnaire will be used to minimize any risk of exercise and ensure the safety of individuals. If any contraindications to exercise are reported in the CSEP Get-Active Questionnaire, prospective participants will be required to obtain clearance from a physician or CSEP-Certified Clinical Exercise Physiologist prior to participation. If payment is required for this clearance, prospective participants will be reimbursed.
* Individuals under the age of 18 will be excluded.
* Individuals who are currently retired are ineligible to participate.
* Individuals who are unable to speak and read English will be excluded for the following reasons: (a) some questionnaires used in the present study do not have validated translations \& (b) feasibility issues with the live translation of QEP sessions.
* Individuals who currently engage in more than 60 minutes of structured exercise per week (assessed using the Stanford Leisure Time Activity Categorical Item) will be excluded.
* Individuals who are currently pregnant will be excluded due to safety risks.
* Individuals who plan to move outside of the province of British Columbia within the next 6 months (during which the trial will be taking place) will be excluded.
